title: Expectations and Adaptation to Environmental Threats
abstract: Scarce information and human capital may make it difficult to form accurate expectations, limiting responses to uncertain environmental threats like air pollution. We study two cross-randomised interventions in Lahore, Pakistan: (i) general training in forecasting and (ii) provision of air pollution forecasts. Both reduced the subjects’ own air pollution forecast errors; the training effect suggests that modest educational interventions can durably improve forecasting skills. Forecast receipt increased demand for protective masks and the responsiveness of outdoor time to pollution. Forecast recipients were willing to pay 41% of their total mobile phone costs for continued access, consistent with welfare gains from adaptation.
abstract_zh: 信息匮乏和人力资本不足，可能使人们难以形成准确的预期，从而限制其对空气污染等不确定环境威胁的应对。我们在巴基斯坦拉合尔开展了两项交叉随机化干预：（i）预测能力的一般培训，以及（ii）提供空气污染预报。两项干预均降低了受试者自身空气污染预测的误差；培训效果表明，适度的教育干预可以持久地提升预测能力。获得预报提高了人们对防护口罩的需求，并使户外活动时间对污染状况的反应更为灵敏。预报接受者愿意为持续获取该服务支付其手机总费用的41%，这与适应行为带来福利增益的结论相一致。

abstract: Does the identity of an information provider affect consumers’ demand for environmental information? In a randomized experiment in Lahore, Pakistan, we provide identical day-ahead air quality SMS forecasts to 1,010 households, varying only whether the source is attributed to a government agency or an NGO. Subjects exhibit high willingness to pay for the service---roughly equivalent to one month of mobile data services---yet despite evidence from other domains that provider identity shapes uptake, we find no difference in willingness to pay across sources, a precisely estimated null (95% CI: [$-$6.9, 7.5] PKR, ruling out differences larger than 3% of mean WTP). Subjects do, however, perceive government forecasts as less accurate, suggesting limited demand for accuracy at the margin. Donation games reveal that subjects prefer their assigned source and value service attributes beyond accuracy, particularly reliability. Our findings imply that expanding the supply of accessible environmental information in developing economies can generate welfare gains regardless of which entity provides it, provided the service is delivered reliably.
abstract_zh: 信息提供者的身份是否会影响消费者对环境信息的需求？在巴基斯坦拉合尔的一项随机实验中，我们向1010户家庭提供了内容完全相同的次日空气质量短信预报，仅改变信息来源的归属，即归因于政府机构或非政府组织（NGO）。受试者对该服务表现出较高的支付意愿，大致相当于一个月的移动数据服务费用；然而，尽管其他领域的证据表明，提供者身份会影响采纳率，我们却发现不同来源之间的支付意愿并无差异，这是一个估计精确的零结果（95%置信区间：[-6.9, 7.5]巴基斯坦卢比，可排除超过平均支付意愿3%的差异）。不过，受试者确实认为政府预报的准确性较低，这表明在边际上对准确性的需求有限。捐赠博弈显示，受试者更偏好其被分配的信息来源，并且看重准确性之外的服务属性，尤其是可靠性。我们的研究结果表明，在发展中经济体扩大可获取的环境信息供给，只要服务能够可靠地提供，无论由哪一主体提供，都能带来福利增益。
